title: v1/chat.completions: add response_mode param, role-alias mapping, and logprob sanitizer
author: Marcel Ortega
description: Motivation: bring /v1/chat.completions parity improvements for downstream OpenAI-compatible clients. This PR introduces a lightweight response_mode parameter that controls top-level framing ("text" | "json-framed" | "structured"), centralizes role aliasing for backwards-compatible role names, and implements a sanitizer pass for logprobs/stop reconciliation to avoid leaking token indices in streaming fallbacks. Changes are conservative and guarded behind compat flags by default. The description below summarizes intent, scope, runtime implications, and migration notes.
commits: a1f3d9c: introduce response_mode enum and basic mapping in openai_compat layer
b4e7f21: add role_alias table and lookup tests
c3b5528: implement logprob_sanitizer pass in streaming runtime with unit tests
d9f88ab: SDK: expose response_mode enum in Python/TS clients
e2a5f10: docs: document response_mode behaviors and migration guide
f7c1c55: fix flakiness in test_openai_compat by allowing slight token delta
review_comments: Tina Chen (reviewer): The response_mode enum is helpful but we need explicit guidance on how cached prefix KV gets serialized in 'json-framed' mode. Can we add an integration test?

Marcel Ortega (author): Added integration test and a comment in param_mapper explaining the KV serialization behavior. The integration test lives in tests/test_openai_compat.py and exercises both cached and uncached flows.
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Logprob sanitizer looks reasonable but the C++ implementation uses an extra heap allocation path on hot code. Can you refactor to reuse the existing buffer?
Marcel Ortega (author): Refactored to reuse streaming buffer and added a microbenchmark showing <2% overhead on P40 compared to baseline.
Priya Desai (approver): Tests and docs look good. Please ensure SDK enums are stable strings for compatibility before merging.
release_notes: - Added response_mode param to openai compatibility layer: controls top-level framing semantics (text | json-framed | structured). - Added role aliasing table to normalize legacy role names (e.g., assistant->system-assistant aliases supported). - Implemented logprob sanitizer to reconcile stop boundaries and avoid exposing token indices in streaming fallbacks.
migration_notes: Clients that depend on exact framing should opt-in to response_mode="json-framed"; default behavior remains text to preserve existing integrations. SDKs expose stable string enums; update pinned SDKs if you use new modes.
notes_for_sre: Monitor compat_response_mode.* metrics added to observability. Watch for increased streaming latency on high-concurrency workloads; microbenchmark indicates <2% overhead but we rolled this behind a feature flag initially.
